A government-built community toilet for women was allegedly occupied by a father-son duo since 2022. They refused to unlock it despite repeated notices from the district administration, the officials said on Wednesday.
The Koirona police station on October 14, Tuesday, registered a case based on a complaint from Kudi Khurd village head Rinku Mishra against Omkar Nath Tiwari and his son Tribhuvan Nath Tiwari alias Nachkau Tiwari.
Manish Dwivedi, the Koirona police station in-charge, said that a case has been registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Sections 318 and 319 (cheating), 336, 338, 340 (forgery), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace) and 351 (criminal intimidation) and legal proceedings are unwerway.
The district panchayati raj officer Sanjay Mishra said that after the village head lodged a complaint, they approached the superintendent of police and the district magistrate.
The local lekhpal conducted an inquiry and the tehsildar confirmed that the two-seater government toilet was locked. Senior officials took action and issued notices directing the duo to open it immediately.
Mishra alleged that on August 1, 2026, that when Rinku Mishra asked the father and son to unlock the toilet, they abused the village head and her husband Ravindra Kumar Mishra. The duo also allegedly assaulted them with sticks before driving them away.
Mishra added that Omkar Nath Tiwari claimed that there was no encroachment and the toilet was unlocked in an affidavit he submitted to the panchayati raj department on September 30, The affidavit purportedly carried the signature of a villager, Rajbali Bharatiya.
Women from the village approached the department after the affidavit was submitted, alleging that Bharatiya was illiterate and used his thumb impression instead of signing documents.
When Bharatiya denied signing it or submitting any such document when he was called to verify the affidavit.
Mishra ordered the registration of a case against the father and son on October 12 for allegedly submitting a forged affidavit to continue occupying government property.
The police said efforts are being made to reopen the toilet for public use.

With temperatures rising over the past few days, the Panvel Municipal Corporation has urged residents to take precautions against heat-related illnesses, including heatstroke and dehydration.
In an advisory issued on Wednesday, the civic body appealed to citizens to avoid stepping out during peak sunlight hours, stay hydrated and take extra care of vulnerable groups, particularly young children, senior citizens and people working outdoors.
Panvel civic body issues heatwave safety guidelines
Dr Anand Gosavi, Chief Medical Officer of the Panvel Municipal Corporation, advised residents to carry water while travelling, wear light-coloured, loose-fitting cotton clothes and use hats, umbrellas or sunglasses when venturing outdoors.
"Residents should avoid going out in the scorching sun as far as possible. If stepping out is necessary, they should take adequate precautions and drink sufficient water at regular intervals to prevent dehydration," Dr Gosavi said.

Santiago declares red alert over thunderstorm and hail — The Rio Times
On October 13, 2026, Chile’s National Disaster Prevention and Response Service, Senapred, declared a red alert for the Santiago Metropolitan Region due to a thunderstorm, heavy rain and hail. The severe weather caused road flooding in several parts of the capital, power outages and restrictions to metro operations.
According to The Rio Times, as of 5:00 p.m. local time, around 36,000 customers remained without electricity. Reports cited figures ranging from 36,155 to 36,928 subscribers, while Diario Financiero later reported that more than 40,000 households were without power.
Flooding and metro restrictions
Hail covered the streets of Santiago, while flooding was recorded, in particular, in the communes of Providencia, Ñuñoa, Las Condes and La Reina. The areas with the highest number of power outages included Quilicura, Quinta Normal, Providencia, Lampa, Pudahuel, Peñalolén, Colina, La Reina and Estación Central.
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.
Metro de Santiago closed some station entrances due to the rain. Pedro de Valdivia station on Line 1 was closed because of water accumulation, while passengers were no longer allowed to enter at Salvador station. On Line 2, service was restricted on the Hospital El Pino–Franklin and Los Héroes–Vespucio Norte sections.
Warning for the country’s central region
Chile’s National Meteorological Service issued a warning of hazardous weather conditions for seven regions in the central part of the country. It concerned intense precipitation, unstable weather and thunderstorms throughout the evening.
The Sernageomin Geological Service assessed the risk of landslides and mudflows in the foothills of Santiago as moderate or high. Diario Financiero also reported that hail could threaten agricultural production in the region. At the time of publication, there were no reports of injuries or deaths.
